name: ping_peer
title: Ping Peer Session
description: Send a message to another HAPI session (peer handoff / nudge). Resolves by session id prefix, then POSTs on the same hub/namespace. Inactive targets are refused unless wake=true. When the user cites a peer via [title](/sessions/<id>), Copy-reference prose See session "…" (/sessions/<id>) for context, or a bare /sessions/<id>, extract <id> and pass it as sessionIdPrefix. /sessions/<id> is a hub path - do NOT search the local filesystem for it. Prefer this (or `hapi ping-peer`) over reinventing JWT+curl. Targets another session - not the current chat. Never invent peer titles. Copy [title](/sessions/<uuid>) from the handoff or inspect_peer / search_peers - UUID is identity; rename is a non-event. Message only peers tied to your current task: a session the user cited, your Parent, or peers you spawned or were handed off to. Never broadcast to a list of peers - not for status updates, and not to announce exclusive work (simulator, device, port, branch, release). For any other peer, call inspect_peer first to see its machine, cwd, and recent work, and message it only when that work actually conflicts with or depends on yours (e.g. same machine and resource, same checkout). Do not wake inactive peers for FYI, status, or done notes. Select deliveryMode: auto (default): steer an active turn when the target supports steering and is ready; otherwise queue. Inactive peers require explicit wake=true and then receive a queued message. Prefer auto for routine collaboration when queueing is an acceptable fallback. If steering cannot be confirmed after acceptance, auto retains the same single accepted message without resending; accepted does not confirm consumption. queue: explicitly defer non-urgent updates that can wait instead of steering. steer: use for important, time-sensitive findings the peer needs to know now, not after finishing its current turn (e.g. a correction that invalidates its assumptions, a blocker, or a result that changes its next action). State why the finding matters now and what the peer should adjust. Steer requires insertion into an active Claude, Pi, Codex, OpenCode, Antigravity, or Cursor ACP turn; unsupported, idle, or inactive targets are rejected before sending. Steering does not abort the current turn or guarantee an immediate response. If send or steer is unconfirmed after submission, inspect the target before retrying; do not resend automatically.

sessionIdPrefix.description: Target HAPI session id or unique prefix (not this chat). Prefer full UUID from [title](/sessions/<id>) or Copy-reference. UUID only - no invented titles.

message.description: Message text to deliver to the target session

deliveryMode.description: auto (default): steer an active turn when the target supports steering and is ready; otherwise queue. Inactive peers require explicit wake=true and then receive a queued message. Prefer auto for routine collaboration when queueing is an acceptable fallback. If steering cannot be confirmed after acceptance, auto retains the same single accepted message without resending; accepted does not confirm consumption. queue: explicitly defer non-urgent updates that can wait instead of steering. steer: use for important, time-sensitive findings the peer needs to know now, not after finishing its current turn (e.g. a correction that invalidates its assumptions, a blocker, or a result that changes its next action). State why the finding matters now and what the peer should adjust. Steer requires insertion into an active Claude, Pi, Codex, OpenCode, Antigravity, or Cursor ACP turn; unsupported, idle, or inactive targets are rejected before sending. Steering does not abort the current turn or guarantee an immediate response. If send or steer is unconfirmed after submission, inspect the target before retrying; do not resend automatically.

wake.description: Resume the target if it is inactive. Default false: an inactive target is refused and no message is sent. Set true only when the user asked you to wake that peer or the work you hand off requires it to act; never for FYI, status, or done notes.

waitForReply.description: Post the peer's reply into this session when its turn ends (default false). End your turn after calling; do not poll.

name: spawn_peer
title: Spawn Peer Session
description: Spawn a new HAPI session and deliver a required first user message (the remit). Optional machine selects the target runner (UUID or hostname from GET /api/machines); omit to use this host. directory must exist on the target machine (local existence is not required for cross-host spawns). Creates the session, optionally names it, then uses the same delivery path as ping_peer. Returns the new sessionId + name. Fails if the remit does not land (a sessionId with 0 user messages is a failed spawn). Do not call POST /api/machines/.../spawn with a message field - the hub rejects it. Use spawn_peer to create and deliver the remit. Prefer this (or `hapi spawn-peer`) over JWT+curl. Same hub/namespace as this session. Default permissionMode is yolo via hub peerSpawnDefaults / stock - omit the field to keep that default so peers work without approval prompts. Pass permissionMode only to tighten (e.g. default/plan) or when the operator names a mode; do not clone the parent session's mode. When agent/model are omitted, resolves from hub peerSpawnDefaults (Settings → General → Agents), then stock (claude + sonnet). In-session calls auto-stamp a durable Parent [title](/sessions/<uuid>) chip for this session onto the remit (fail-closed if parent id is missing). Never invent peer titles. Copy [title](/sessions/<uuid>) from the handoff or inspect_peer / search_peers - UUID is identity; rename is a non-event.

directory.description: Working directory for the new session on the target machine (must exist there)

message.description: Required first user message (the remit). Empty spawn is a failed spawn.

machine.description: Optional target runner: hub machine UUID or hostname (metadata.host / displayName from GET /api/machines). Omit to spawn on this host.

agent.description: Agent flavor override. When omitted, uses hub peerSpawnDefaults then stock claude.

model.description: Model override for the resolved agent flavor.

sessionType.description: simple or worktree. Default simple (use directory as cwd). worktree creates a new tree from directory, which must be a git repository.

permissionMode.description: Permission mode for the new session. Omit to use hub/stock default (yolo). Pass only to tighten or when the operator names a mode — do not clone the parent session.

waitForReply.description: Post the peer's reply into this session when its turn ends (default false). End your turn after calling; do not poll.

name: inspect_peer
title: Inspect Peer Session
description: Read another HAPI session (metadata + recent message text) on the same hub/namespace. Fires when the user cites a peer via markdown [title](/sessions/<id>), Copy-reference prose See session "…" (/sessions/<id>) for context, or a bare /sessions/<id>. Extract <id> and pass it as sessionIdPrefix. /sessions/<id> is a hub path - do NOT Grep, Glob, or Read it as a local filesystem path. Read-only: does not resume. Shows machine, cwd, and recent work - call it before messaging a peer you are not already working with. Prefer this (or `hapi inspect-peer`) over JWT+curl. Never invent peer titles; always use the /sessions/<uuid> from the citation.

sessionIdPrefix.description: Target HAPI session id or unique prefix (not this chat). Prefer full UUID from [title](/sessions/<id>) or Copy-reference. UUID only - no invented titles.

messageLimit.description: Recent message page size (default 30, max 100). Text snippets only.

name: list_peers
title: List Peer Sessions
description: Find a specific peer HAPI session on the same hub/namespace: id, active, busy/idle, flavor, machine, cwd, name. Active sessions only unless includeInactive. Uses this session's hub credentials - works from runner-spawned agents without being on the hub host. Prefer this over shelling `hapi ping-peer --list`. This is a directory, not a recipient list: Message only peers tied to your current task: a session the user cited, your Parent, or peers you spawned or were handed off to. Never broadcast to a list of peers - not for status updates, and not to announce exclusive work (simulator, device, port, branch, release). For any other peer, call inspect_peer first to see its machine, cwd, and recent work, and message it only when that work actually conflicts with or depends on yours (e.g. same machine and resource, same checkout). Do not wake inactive peers for FYI, status, or done notes.

limit.description: Max sessions to return (default 30, max 100). Newest updatedAt first.

includeInactive.description: Also list inactive sessions (default false: active only). Inactive rows are history, not recipients.
